nodes.title: SG-2 Typed asset manifest and validated content schemas
nodes.body:
Context: game/ has YAML-based content (game/src/content/loader.ts) and a hardcoded ASSET_PATHS/HOTSPOTS map in game/frontend/src/runtime/assets.ts. Desired behavior: typed interfaces plus zod validators for the asset manifest and world objects, scene/location content under game/src/content/worlds/the-boys-room, the asset folder tree, and a loader that reports missing assets without crashing. Why: future AI cycles can add or replace assets without rewriting the engine.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a manifest and world content, When validated, Then typed zod schemas accept valid data and reject invalid data with path-specific errors
- Given a manifest reference to a file that does not exist, When the loader runs, Then it reports the asset as missing and does not throw
- Given the repo, When listing game/public/assets, Then worlds/the-boys-room/{backgrounds,furniture,objects,characters,effects,audio} and ui/{icons,frames,cursors} exist


## Scope
- In scope: zod schemas and TS types
- In scope: the-boys-room content files
- In scope: asset folder tree
- In scope: manifest loader and unit tests
- Out of scope: Phaser rendering
- Out of scope: new artwork
- Out of scope: UI changes
- Preserve: existing game/content YAML loader and its tests
- Preserve: game/frontend runtime behavior


## Technical constraints
- TypeScript with zod runtime validators
- content separate from engine


## Definition of done
- All requirements, Act and Verify units complete


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Typed manifest and object schemas with runtime validators
nodes.body:
Context: no manifest or object schema exists. Desired behavior: AssetManifest records id, path, type, dimensions, spritesheet frames, animations, origin/anchor and interaction bounds; object schema covers position, scale, layer, bounds, actions, visibility conditions and persistent-state fields. Why: single validated contract for content.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a valid manifest entry for each asset type, When parsed, Then it succeeds and returns typed data
- Given an entry with missing id, negative dimensions or unknown type, When parsed, Then it fails naming the offending field path
- Given a world object with position, scale, layer, bounds, actions, visibleWhen and persistentState, When parsed, Then it succeeds; an unknown layer fails


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/manifest schemas and types
- Out of scope: loader
- Out of scope: content data
- Preserve: game/src/state/types.ts


## Technical constraints
- zod added to game/package.json


## Definition of done
- Schemas and inferred types exported


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Manifest loader validates references and reports missing assets without crashing
nodes.body:
Context: no manifest loader exists. Desired behavior: loadManifest validates data, checks every object asset reference exists in the manifest (dangling) and every manifest path exists via an injected exists function, returning a report and fallback entries instead of throwing. Why: missing assets must not crash the game.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a manifest whose file is missing, When loaded, Then report.missing lists its id and the call does not throw
- Given an object referencing an unknown asset id, When loaded, Then report.dangling lists it
- Given invalid manifest data, When loaded, Then report.errors is non-empty and no exception propagates
- Given a missing asset, When resolving it, Then the fallback entry is returned


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts
- Out of scope: Phaser loading
- Preserve: existing loader.ts


## Technical constraints
- Filesystem access via injected exists function


## Dependencies
- R1
- R2


## Definition of done
- Loader implemented


## Clarifying questions
- None

acceptance_criteria: Schemas export parse-able validators and inferred types
zod is declared in game/package.json

steps.action: Add "zod": "^3.23.0" to dependencies next to yaml, then run npm install in game/ to update package-lock.json

Create schemas. assetEntry: id (non-empty string), path (non-empty string), type enum background|furniture|object|spritesheet|effect|audio|icon|frame|cursor, width/height positive ints optional, frames {frameWidth,frameHeight,count} optional, animations record of {frames:number[],frameRate:number positive,repeat:int>=-1} optional, origin {x,y} 0..1 default {0.5,0.5}, interactionBounds {x,y,width,height} optional. manifest: {version:1, assets: array}. worldObject: id, name, asset (string), position {x,y}, scale number positive default 1, layer enum background|furniture|objects|characters|effects|ui, bounds optional, actions array of enum inspect|push|search|leave, visibleWhen optional array of {flag,equals?}|{hasItem}, persistentState optional {flag:string, openAsset?:string}. scene: {id,title,objects:worldObject[]}
Export types via z.infer of the four schemas from schema.ts

nodes.summary: loadManifest with reference validation and fallbacks
acceptance_criteria: Returns report with errors, dangling, missing
resolveAsset returns fallback for missing

steps.action: Export loadManifest(manifestData: unknown, scene: unknown, exists: (assetPath:string)=>boolean): {manifest: AssetManifest|null; scene: SceneContent|null; errors: string[]; missing: string[]; dangling: {objectId:string; asset:string}[]}. Use safeParse for both; on failure push `path: message` strings to errors. For each manifest asset where !exists(path) push id to missing. For each scene object whose asset is not a manifest id push to dangling. Wrap in try/catch to never throw. Export FALLBACK_ASSET (id 'fallback', type 'object', path 'ui/frames/fallback.png') and resolveAsset(report, id) returning the manifest entry or FALLBACK_ASSET when id is missing from manifest or in report.missing
